title: The Benchmark Database — JSON Record Serialization Throughput
body: Public edition. Public knowledge, fact-checked reference. Benchmark: JSON Record Serialization Throughput. Target: database record write path (object -> JSON string) Metric: records serialized per second; total ms for N records Methodology: Build N=20000 records with fixed seed; JSON.stringify each; assert byte length > 0 and a spot record round-trips exactly. Scoring: Higher records/sec is better. Pass: all records serialize and spot round-trip matches. How to run: save the record program as bench.js and run: node bench.js. The program executes the benchmark, checks its own assertions, and prints a RESULT line with the measured values. How to read results: records_per_sec (or the per-benchmark unit) is the measured throughput on the build machine; assertions listed under recorded_results all passed. Beginner exercise: run the program twice and compare the measured timings — correctness assertions must pass both times while timings vary slightly. Advanced pattern: use this benchmark as a regression gate — re-run after any change to the measured operation and compare against the recorded results.

Scoring: Higher texts/sec is better. Pass: token checksums agree. How to run: save the record program as bench.js and run: node bench.js. The program executes the benchmark, checks its own assertions, and prints a RESULT line with the measured values. How to read results: records_per_sec (or the per-benchmark unit) is the measured throughput on the build machine; assertions listed under recorded_results all passed. Beginner exercise: run the program twice and compare the measured timings — correctness assertions must pass both times while timings vary slightly. Advanced pattern: use this benchmark as a regression gate — re-run after any change to the measured operation and compare against the recorded results.
